name: Electrothermal Chemical Carbine ETCC-5 'Flashpoint'
description:
The ETCC-5 uses electrothermal-chemical propulsion, a system in which a high-voltage electrical discharge is injected directly into a liquid propellant plasma behind the projectile at the moment of firing. The electrical discharge — generated by a capacitor bank integrated into the weapon's fore-end — converts a small volume of liquid propellant into a plasma jet approximately 40 times more energetically dense than conventional propellant gases. This allows the ETCC-5 to drive a standard 8.6mm projectile to approximately 1,850 m/s from a 420mm barrel, producing muzzle energies that exceed most dedicated anti-materiel rifles while maintaining a package compact enough for two-handed field use.

The weapon's plasma generation creates a distinctive secondary effect: a brief, intense flash of blue-white light exits the muzzle at the moment of discharge, visible in peripheral vision at ranges up to 300 meters. This 'Flashpoint' signature is the weapon's most recognizable characteristic and its primary tactical liability. Operators in the field report that the flash is disorienting to targets at close range and has caused temporary photoreceptor disruption in unshielded observers within 50 meters, an unintended secondary effect that ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC has since studied for deliberate exploitation in newer variants. The flash also makes the shooter's position immediately obvious, which has driven extensive tactical doctrine around single-shot engagements and immediate repositioning.

The liquid propellant system uses a sealed, pressurized 40mL cartridge that feeds a 10-round magazine of standard 8.6mm projectiles. Each shot consumes approximately 3mL of propellant, giving each cartridge 13 shots before the propellant is exhausted — slightly more than the magazine capacity, meaning operators typically exhaust ammunition before propellant. The capacitor bank recharges from a rail-mounted power cell between shots, producing a 1.4-second cycling delay that defines the weapon's semi-automatic, deliberate-fire character.
specifications:
caliber: 8.6x70mm ETC-spec projectile
feed system: 10-round box magazine, 40mL liquid propellant cartridge (integrated)
muzzle velocity: 1,850 m/s
muzzle energy: ~14,200 J
effective range: 800m (personnel), 400m (light vehicle armor)
cyclic rate: Semi-automatic, 1.4s capacitor recharge between shots
weight: 4.1 kg with magazine, 4.7 kg with optics package
dimensions: 760mm length (fixed stock), 420mm barrel
power source: Integrated 72V capacitor bank, powered by 24V rail cell (30 shots per cell)
secondary effect: Blue-white muzzle flash, photoreceptor disruption risk within 50m
tactical_use: The ETCC-5 is deployed as a precision anti-materiel and anti-personnel rifle where conventional high-caliber weapons would be logistically impractical. Its liquid propellant system eliminates spent brass and produces minimal acoustic signature compared to conventional equivalents, though the muzzle flash negates most of the concealment benefit. Military operators use it for vehicle window defeat, light drone interdiction, and hardened-target precision fire. The 1.4-second cycling delay requires trained trigger discipline — operators are taught to fire, reacquire, and fire again rather than attempting rapid follow-up shots. Special operations units have developed a two-person team doctrine where a spotter calls target transitions to compensate for the inter-shot delay.
cultural_context: The ETCC-5 is almost entirely absent from civilian GLMZ life — its military-only designation is genuinely enforced, and the liquid propellant cartridges are serialized and tracked. When one appears outside military hands, it is significant news. In the city's underground arms trade, a single ETCC-5 commands prices that reflect not just its performance but the risk of possessing it. Military deserters sometimes surface one, and the occasional black-market unit has been traced to ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC's own internal security personnel. The weapon's distinctive blue muzzle flash has entered urban mythology — stories of 'the blue gun' circulate in lower-tier arcology communities as a warning about something dangerous and governmental passing through.
known_users: Arms dealers specializing in military surplus (possession only, rarely fired)
story_hooks: Three ETCC-5 units have gone missing from a military depot and the serial numbers have been scrubbed — someone inside the logistics chain is selling to a buyer who needs precision fire capability without the military connection

A witness reports seeing the blue flash signature in the direction of a political assassination, but the official investigation insists the weapon used was conventional — someone is lying about the ballistics report
ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC wants to recover a prototype ETCC-5 variant that was taken during a research facility breach before competitors can reverse-engineer the plasma generation system

A former military sniper now operating as a freelancer has an ETCC-5 and is willing to sell — but the buyer realizes the weapon's serial number matches one reported destroyed three years ago in a classified incident

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular carbine with a pronounced forward-swept profile dominated by a large cylindrical capacitor housing integrated into the fore-end. The weapon presents an aggressive, high-tech aesthetic — part precision rifle, part energy weapon — with a tapered barrel and aggressive muzzle brake. The stock is streamlined and compact, suggesting military ergonomics optimized for rapid repositioning.
physical_description.dimensions: 760mm overall length, 420mm barrel, approximately 65mm width at the capacitor housing, 45mm height at receiver
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial but not unwieldy — 4.1 kg creates a deliberate, planted feel in the hands. The weight is front-biased due to the capacitor bank and liquid propellant cartridge, creating a natural downward cant that aids in rapid target acquisition.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade carbon composite chassis with steel receiver core and titanium barrel. The capacitor housing is hard-anodized aluminum with embedded cooling fins.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray composite with brushed titanium accents along the barrel. The capacitor housing features a dark anodized finish with visible heat dissipation scoring. Worn edges reveal silver undercoat where high-contact points show use.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with silver-titanium barrel, dark gray cooling fins, and amber-tinted pressure gauge on the liquid propellant cartridge. Charging ports glow faintly with inactive blue status LEDs.
physical_description.grip_texture: Aggressively textured rubberized polymer with aggressive crosshatch pattern, wrapped in a thin layer of abraded synthetic cord for secondary grip points. The magazine well is reinforced with knurled steel.
distinctive_features: Large cylindrical capacitor bank integrated into the fore-end with prominent cooling fins and heat vents
Transparent 40mL liquid propellant cartridge chamber showing viscous, slightly luminescent fluid level
Dual amber pressure gauges on cartridge housing — one for propellant, one for capacitor charge state
Exposed charging contacts along the rail system with faint blue LED status indicators
Muzzle brake designed to channel the distinctive blue-white plasma discharge, with micro-faceted reflective interior
Recessed magazine catch and magazine well with reinforced steel locking lugs
Serial plate and ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC dragon symbol etched into the receiver
Rail-mounted charging port with weathersealed connector cap (frequently worn or missing in field units)
Impact scarring and micro-fractures in the composite stock and fore-end — evidence of field deployment
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC logo — a stylized dragon coiled around an electrical discharge symbol — stamped into the upper receiver. Serial number and 'ETCC-5 FLASHPOINT' designation etched in white fill on the left side of the stock. Capacity ratings and safety warnings in English, Mandarin, and Japanese printed on the cartridge housing.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but maintained. Composite shows minor gouging and impact scarring. The muzzle brake exhibits heat discoloration — faint rainbow oxidation from repeated plasma discharge. The propellant cartridge is frequently replaced, showing connector wear. Charging contacts show oxidation patterns from exposure to Great Lakes humidity. Stock and grip show signs of hard use and tactical repositioning — scuffed finishes, stress fractures in non-critical areas.
